name: Why Can't You Just Be Normal
look: Two stacked panels inside a car. Top: a haggard woman with messy blonde hair turns around from the front seat and yells, captioned "Why cant you just be normal?". Bottom: a curly-haired boy in a dark cardigan, belted into the back seat, screams back, captioned "*Screams*".
text: Why cant you just be normal?
use: The mother stands for someone asking a person to act normal, and the screaming kid is whoever answers with something even stranger. Labels name the two sides, and the scream line is often swapped for a specific weird noise or habit.
slots: label on the yelling mother (who wants normal)
examples: My dog when the doorbell rings
Me typing a word I use every day
describe: mom yelling why can't you just be normal at a kid in the car
woman screaming from the front seat and boy screaming in the back
angry mother turns around in the car and her son screams back
curly haired kid shrieking in the backseat
two panel car scene where mom and child both yell
origin: Uses two stills from a car scene in the 2014 Australian horror film The Babadook.
